author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell looks back 23 years to his time in treatment, and pinpoints the exact moment that made him feel most exposed, not the hard days, but the mandatory group outings, being loaded onto a bus with everyone else and taken somewhere like a bowling alley or a go kart track, with absolutely no way to hide or explain away why you're all there together. From there the conversation widens into something bigger, Russell's belief that everyone is either moving toward God or away from him, and that the people who hit a visible, dramatic rock bottom aren't necessarily any more broken than everyone else quietly trapped by more socially acceptable addictions and false idols. A reflective, honest look at vulnerability, faith, and what recovery actually asks of you.

author: Russell Brand
description:
David Morens, Fauci's senior advisor for nearly two decades, just pleaded guilty to a federal conspiracy charge tied to hiding Covid research records from public records requests. Russell breaks down what that reveals about the machinery working around Fauci during the pandemic, before turning to something even stranger, entries from Fauci's own personal diary showing him seemingly delighted by his sudden fame, including comments about actress Julia Roberts that don't exactly match the cold, purely clinical public image he was known for. Russell can't resist a dark joke or two along the way, comparing the carefully managed image to something out of a very different kind of history. A candid, unsettling look at the gap between the persona and the man behind it.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Nathan Apfel admits he almost wrote off Russell's book the second he heard the title, expecting it to be exactly the kind of thing he'd usually roll his eyes at. Instead he found himself completely won over, especially by Russell's breakdown of Christ's final words on the cross, "it is finished," a phrase Russell says he couldn't bring himself to fully believe for 35 years. The conversation deepens from there, touching on the false identity Russell says he spent his whole life building, a golden calf he calls it, and the moment it all came crashing down at the exact same time his infant son was undergoing open heart surgery. A genuinely moving conversation about doubt, belief, and what actually matters when everything else falls away.
